assignments.title: Assignment 1
assignments.topic: Introduction to Public Speaking & The Canons of Rhetoric

questions.question: Public Speaking is a skill that cannot be acquired.
questions.explanation: Public speaking is not purely an innate talent; it is an acquired skill that can be developed and mastered through study, practice, and constructive feedback.

questions.question: According to Ralph Waldo Emerson, “Speech is power: speech is to persuade, to convert, to compel.”
questions.explanation: Ralph Waldo Emerson famously observed that speech is power: speech is to persuade, to convert, to compel an audience.

questions.question: A rhetorical device is a technique that is used by a speaker or an author for conveying a particular message to the audience in such a way that it provokes an emotional response to a particular action.
questions.explanation: Rhetorical devices use stylistic language to evoke emotion, emphasize key themes, and move listeners toward a specific response or action.

questions.question: Listening is the ability to accurately receive only.
questions.explanation: Listening involves far more than merely receiving audio signals; it entails comprehending, evaluating, interpreting, and responding to spoken communication.

questions.question: Incremental Plagiarism is stealing excerpts from multiple sources and combining them into your personal speech.
questions.explanation: Patchwork (mosaic) plagiarism is stitching excerpts from multiple sources into a speech. Incremental plagiarism occurs when a speaker fails to give credit for specific borrowed quotes or paraphrases.

questions.question: Which one of the given options is incorrect about ways of being ethical?
questions.explanation: Alienating the audience goes against ethical public speaking. Ethical communication requires building bridges, respecting listeners, and fostering mutual trust.

questions.question: Which one is not a caution during speech delivery?
questions.explanation: Bringing in the bigger picture is a desirable speech practice that provides broad context and significance, rather than an error to avoid.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the characteristic of a good listener?
options: Paying attention to the speaker during the limited time of speech
Listening to the speaker with presumptions and biases
Indulging in other activities while speech is delivered
questions.explanation: Active listening requires setting aside distractions and biases to dedicate full attention to the speaker's message during the presentation.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a speech by Martin Luther King Jr.?
questions.explanation: 'I Have a Dream' is the landmark civil rights speech delivered by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. in Washington D.C. in 1963. ('Tryst with Destiny' was by Jawaharlal Nehru; 'O Captain! My Captain!' is by Walt Whitman).

questions.question: According to Quintilian, there are five canons of Rhetoric for curating a persuasive speech. Pick the right combination.
questions.explanation: The five classical canons of rhetoric formulated by Roman rhetoricians (including Quintilian and Cicero) are Invention (inventio), Disposition (dispositio), Style (elocutio), Memorization (memoria), and Delivery (pronuntiatio).

assignments.title: Assignment 2
assignments.topic: Audience Analysis, Relevance Theory & Speaking Aids

questions.question: Daniel Sperber and Deirdre Wilson propounded the relevance theory.
questions.explanation: Dan Sperber and Deirdre Wilson published 'Relevance: Communication and Cognition' in 1986, establishing Relevance Theory in pragmatics.

questions.question: People in a group have an increased sense of responsibility.
questions.explanation: In group settings, individuals often experience diffusion of responsibility or social loafing, leading to a decreased individual sense of accountability.

questions.question: A speaking outline is a fairly condensed version of a formal written outline.
questions.explanation: A speaking outline is a concise, condensed guide with keywords and delivery cues, designed to prompt the speaker without reading word-for-word.

questions.question: Oration requires both short-term as well as long-term memory.
questions.explanation: Speakers rely on long-term memory for organized knowledge, evidence, and narratives, and short-term working memory to adapt to real-time audience cues and immediate phrasing.

questions.question: Microphones and Speakers are the basic technological tools for public speaking.
questions.explanation: Microphones and loudspeakers serve as the core electroacoustic amplification tools enabling speakers to project clearly across diverse venues.

questions.question: Greater the positive cognitive effects, greater will be its ______.
questions.explanation: In Relevance Theory, communication achieves higher cognitive relevance when it produces greater positive cognitive effects with minimal processing effort.

questions.question: ______ audience demands factual and evidence-based argument.
questions.explanation: A directive audience requires concrete data, rigorous logic, and verifiable evidence to be convinced and take decisive action.

questions.question: ______ helps to make fluent and timely presentation.
questions.explanation: Speaking index cards provide concise reminders and time markers that allow the speaker to stay fluent, natural, and punctual.

questions.question: The word personality derives its origin from Latin word persona meaning ______.
questions.explanation: The Latin word 'persona' referred to the theatrical mask worn by actors in classical drama to project a role and amplify the voice.

questions.question: ______ oratory includes live streaming, virtual meetings and webinars.
questions.explanation: Digital oratory encompasses all speech delivered through computer-mediated interfaces, web broadcasts, and interactive teleconferencing.

questions.question: According to Lev Vygotsky, which of the following are the frameworks for humans to experience and understand reality?
questions.explanation: In Lev Vygotsky's sociocultural framework, language and culture are the primary socio-semiotic tools through which humans perceive, construct, and understand reality.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is not true about the nature of Anxiety?
options: It is characterized by cognitive, somatic, emotional and behavioral components.
It inhibits the secretion of the hormone adrenaline in our body.
questions.explanation: Anxiety triggers the autonomic sympathetic nervous system, stimulating the rapid secretion of adrenaline (epinephrine) rather than inhibiting it.

questions.question: According to Mulac and Sherman, which of the following is/are among the four elements of speech fright?
questions.explanation: Mulac and Sherman (1974) identified behavioral elements of speech fright including dysfluency (speech disruption) and behavioral inhibition.

questions.question: Glossophobia is derived from the Greek word ‘glossa’ which means
questions.explanation: 'Glossa' is the Greek word for tongue. Combined with 'phobos' (fear), glossophobia literally denotes fear of the tongue, universally used for speech anxiety.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about ABC Model of Communication Attitude?
options: It was first formulated by American psychologist, Albert Ellis.
The acronym stands for its three key components – Attitudes, Belief, Consequences.
The acronym stands for its three key components – Affect, Behavior, Cognition.
questions.explanation: Albert Ellis introduced the ABC framework in cognitive therapy, and communication attitude theory structures human attitude along Affect, Behavior, and Cognition, making all options relevant facets of the ABC paradigm.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false. To cast a good first impression as a public speaker, it is imperative to align your appearance with the message of your talk.
questions.explanation: Visual presentation and grooming establish instant credibility (ethos); aligning attire with topic and audience expectations creates positive rapport.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false. The approach of Desensitization is known to aggravate the fear of public speaking.
questions.explanation: Systematic desensitization is an established behavioral therapy that relieves and diminishes public speaking fear through gradual exposure and counter-conditioning.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false. Goleman’s Emotional Competence Framework suggests that emotional competence is composed of cognitive competence and professional competence.
questions.explanation: Daniel Goleman's Emotional Competence Framework splits emotional intelligence into Personal Competence (self-awareness, self-management) and Social Competence (social awareness, relationship management).

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false. The Power of Positive Thinking, a book on the importance of positive attitude in life, is authored by Norman Vincent Peale.
questions.explanation: 'The Power of Positive Thinking' was written by Dr. Norman Vincent Peale and published in 1952.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false. Cognitive development of an individual plays a key role in influencing his/her communicative choices.
questions.explanation: Cognitive maturity dictates perspective-taking, complex semantic selection, and adaptive rhetorical strategies in diverse speaking situations.

questions.question: Every established religion today exists because of the way its preachers address and influence the minds of the masses.
questions.explanation: Oral dissemination, charismatic preaching, and persuasive rhetoric have been historical cornerstones for establishing and sustaining religious movements.

questions.question: Digression is not different from distraction.
questions.explanation: A digression is an intentional, purposeful departure from the central topic used to illuminate an anecdote or re-energize listeners, whereas a distraction is an unintentional loss of focus.

questions.question: Digressions are surprise cards for any speech.
questions.explanation: Well-timed digressions operate like pleasant surprises that keep audiences engaged, break monotony, and offer fresh narrative angles.

questions.question: Child-centered theory was developed by Xingzhi.
questions.explanation: Child-centered pedagogical theory is credited to thinkers such as Jean-Jacques Rousseau and John Dewey; Tao Xingzhi developed Life Education Theory.

questions.question: Which one of the given options is not a type of Vernacular Plays in the European Middle Ages?
questions.explanation: Absurdist drama emerged in the 20th century following World War II, whereas Mystery, Miracle, and Morality plays were the vernacular theatrical forms of medieval Europe.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a component of Classroom Teaching?
questions.explanation: Positive classroom pedagogy relies on psychological safety, motivation, and constructive guidance. Harsh criticism stifles learning and vocal participation.

questions.question: Choose the correct options for types of Dramatic Speeches: (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: In classical drama, the recognized forms of dramatic speech are dialogue, aside, soliloquy, and monologue.

questions.question: Point out the option(s) that correctly match/(es) with the features of Soliloquy. (select all that apply)
options: It is “a long, usually serious spoken discourse that a character in a play delivers to an audience and that reveals the character’s thoughts.”
There is a listener on the stage.
It is not meant for the audience.
Its purpose is to channel the inner thoughts and feelings of the character for the audience.
questions.explanation: A soliloquy is delivered when a character is alone on stage to voice internal contemplations, motives, and emotions directly to the audience.

questions.question: Edward Hall introduced the term kinesics in the year 1952.
questions.explanation: The term 'kinesics' was introduced by Ray Birdwhistell in 1952, whereas Edward T. Hall coined the term 'proxemics'.

questions.question: Communication is only 7% verbal and 93% non-verbal.
questions.explanation: According to Albert Mehrabian's classic study, when communicating emotions and attitudes, 7% is conveyed via spoken words, 38% via tone of voice, and 55% via body language (93% non-verbal).

questions.question: Chronemics is the study of space concerning human communication.
questions.explanation: Chronemics is the study of the role of time in communication; proxemics is the study of space and spatial distance.

questions.question: Memory and attention span are generally limited in public speaking.
questions.explanation: Audience cognitive bandwidth and attention spans are inherently constrained, necessitating concise structures, signposts, and engaging presentation.

questions.question: The aspect of touch has to be dealt with both confidence and caution.
questions.explanation: Haptic communication (touch) carries deep cultural, personal, and professional implications, requiring appropriate confidence and social sensitivity.

questions.question: Under which spatial zone of communication do formal business occasions fall?
questions.explanation: Edward Hall identified Social Space (4 to 12 feet) as the appropriate proxemic zone for impersonal business transactions, committee meetings, and professional interactions.

questions.question: Choose the option that does not determine the communication in low-context cultures.
questions.explanation: Low-context communication relies primarily on explicit verbal messages rather than unspoken hierarchy or social status.

questions.question: Who among the following said that “the man’s boundary begins and ends with his skin”?
questions.explanation: Anthropologist Edward T. Hall explored cultural variations in body buffer zones, contrasting cultures where personal boundary begins and ends with one's skin with those where spatial spheres extend outward.

questions.question: Who introduced the term ‘speech chronemics’?
questions.explanation: H.P. Krüger introduced the concept of speech chronemics to systematically analyze speech timing, tempo, pauses, and pacing in human vocal interactions.

questions.question: For which group among the following is “contact comfort” a primary need?
questions.explanation: Harry Harlow's seminal research demonstrated that physical contact comfort is an essential, primary developmental drive for higher-order mammals.

questions.question: Voice has the potential to reflect the speaker’s ______.
questions.explanation: Vocal inflections, tremors, pitch, and timbre readily reveal a speaker's underlying emotional state and psychological feelings.

questions.question: Inflammation of the larynx, which is one of the common lapses in articulation, is referred to as ______ of the voice.
questions.explanation: Laryngeal inflammation (laryngitis) swells vocal folds and results in hoarseness, causing the voice to sound raspy, breathy, or strained.

questions.question: In ______ reasoning, the conclusion is reached by arriving at a conclusion through observing specific cases, i.e. progression of argument is from specific to general.
questions.explanation: Inductive reasoning moves from specific observed instances to generalized conclusions or probabilistic principles.

questions.question: BATNA (Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement) produces an outcome ______ than the gain expected via negotiation.
questions.explanation: A strong BATNA provides negotiating power because it guarantees a superior alternative if the terms offered at the table fail to meet expectations.

questions.question: The type of debate which is presented before a judge with the power to render a binding decision is categorized as ______.
questions.explanation: Applied debates occur in judicial courts, legislative assemblies, or arbitrations where presiding judges have legal authority to enforce a binding resolution.

questions.question: In the argument of a debate, the statement which the arguer seeks the audience to accept is referred to as the ______ of the argument.
questions.explanation: In argumentation frameworks (e.g., Toulmin's model), the claim is the central assertion or conclusion that the speaker aims to substantiate.

questions.question: The ideal rate of speech delivery is:
questions.explanation: A speaking rate of 130 to 150 words per minute provides the optimal balance of vocal clarity, cognitive processing time, and energetic delivery.

questions.question: The book titled ‘Pragmatics of Human Communication’ is authored by:
questions.explanation: 'Pragmatics of Human Communication' (1967) was written by Paul Watzlawick, Janet Beavin Bavelas, and Don D. Jackson.

questions.question: French philosopher Jacques Derrida argues that any form of communication essentially incorporates a structure of writing for itself. Which term is used to refer to the linguistic field of studying writing systems and their basic components, i.e. graphemes?
questions.explanation: Both 'graphemics' and 'graphematics' refer to the linguistic analysis of writing systems, orthography, and minimal graphic units (graphemes).

questions.question: According to Sir Richard Steele’s views on ideal conversation, as propounded in his essay ‘The Art of Conversation’, which one of the following statement is true?
options: The ideal conversation should not be a laboured one, rather it should be readily and clearly apprehended.
In a conversation, the chief end should be to flaunt eloquence.
Wit is the outcome of much reading but little comprehending.
Conversation ought to be either an attempt to polite sycophancy or of a determined disputation.
questions.explanation: Sir Richard Steele argued that true conversation should flow effortlessly and naturally, being easily understood rather than pedantic, strained, or pretentious.

questions.question: Elocution may be defined as the art of clear and effective expression of thought by speech, intonation and gestures.
questions.explanation: Elocution is the discipline of clear oral articulation, expressive voice modulation, appropriate intonation, and physical gesture in delivery.

questions.question: Every word of more than one syllable has at least one stressed syllable, made prominent by a forceful vocal effort termed as cadence.
questions.explanation: The vocal prominence on a syllable is termed accent or stress. Cadence denotes the melodic rhythm or falling inflective contour of spoken phrases.

questions.question: Assertive sentences usually take a falling tone, except when they do not communicate information or absoluteness.
questions.explanation: Declarative or assertive statements that state definitive facts conclude with a falling intonation contour in standard English.

questions.question: John Donne, an American philosopher proposed the five-step process, known as the Reflective–Thinking Method, for directing discussion in problem-solving groups.
questions.explanation: The Reflective Thinking Method was formulated by American educational philosopher John Dewey (not the 17th-century English poet John Donne).

questions.question: What are the elements of Elocution and Recitation? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Exemplary recitation requires precise accentuation, clear intonation, natural emotional expressiveness, and complementary gesticulation.

questions.question: What does Intonation comprise? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Intonation describes speech melody and changes in pitch, primarily divided into rising tones and falling tones.

questions.question: Speeches about ______ explain how something is made, how something is done, or how something works.
questions.explanation: Informative speeches about processes break down procedural steps, systematic sequences, and operational mechanisms.

questions.question: ______ is the process of creating, reinforcing, or changing people’s beliefs or actions.
questions.explanation: Persuasion is the intentional communication intended to influence, reinforce, or transform attitudes, beliefs, or behaviors.

questions.question: Humour is a mode of communication in which the stimulus produces ______.
questions.explanation: Humor is communicative stimulus designed to evoke laughter, pleasant surprise, and cognitive amusement.

questions.question: Comedy of humour was introduced as a dramatic genre by ______.
questions.explanation: Ben Jonson introduced and popularized the Comedy of Humours during the English Renaissance (e.g. 'Every Man in His Humour').

questions.question: The Latin word ‘humor’ means ______.
questions.explanation: The Latin noun 'humor' means moisture or bodily fluid, rooted in ancient Greek and Roman medicine of the four bodily humors.

questions.question: During an interview session, an interviewee should ______ listen to the questions of the interviewer.
questions.explanation: Active listening ensures that the candidate accurately understands the question's premise before formulating an organized response.

questions.question: Laddering technique is a ______ way of understanding the market choices of consumers.
questions.explanation: Laddering is an in-depth interview technique with a hierarchical probe structure, connecting basic product attributes to personal values.

questions.question: STAR method is suggested to be used in ______ interview.
questions.explanation: The STAR technique (Situation, Task, Action, Result) is widely used to structure compelling answers for behavioral and situational interview questions.

questions.question: Which of the following reasons are responsible for interview bias? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Preconceptions, unconscious stereotyping, and intercultural misunderstandings of non-verbal cues introduce severe interviewer biases.

questions.question: Interview as a process has different applications attached to itself, such as in: (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The interview format is a standard protocol in personnel selection (recruitment) and research qualitative data collection.

questions.question: Levashina and Campion explain Impression Management (IM) as an attempt conscious or unconscious to influence the image during the process of interaction.
questions.explanation: Julia Levashina and Michael Campion defined Impression Management as tactical conscious or unconscious behaviors aimed at shaping how one is perceived.

questions.question: Business conferences enable entrepreneurs to expand network, stimulate new ideas, and create valuable contacts.
questions.explanation: Conferences serve as collaborative platforms facilitating knowledge exchange, professional networking, and strategic venture connections.

questions.question: A discursive conference is organized with an aim to share theoretical or factual information.
questions.explanation: Discursive conferences center on exploratory dialogue, debating opinions, and open discussion rather than unilateral factual transmission.

questions.question: An official list of items of business to be transacted at a particular meeting is termed as minutes of the meeting.
questions.explanation: The planned list of business items is the 'agenda'; the retrospective record of discussions and decisions constitutes the 'minutes'.

questions.question: John Baldoni draws the distinction between leadership and management, in the following terms: “Management is inspiration; leadership is execution.”
questions.explanation: The conventional principle states the opposite: leadership provides vision and inspiration, whereas management handles administration and execution.

questions.question: “Meetings are the fulcrum…the central nervous system of an information society, the centre stage for personal performance.” Who propounded this statement on the nature of meetings?
questions.explanation: George David Kieffer articulated this famous characterization of organizational meetings in 'The Strategy of Meetings'.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a purpose of drafting the agenda of the meeting?
options: To define the purpose of the meeting
To plan the meeting content and flow
To assign responsibility to personals for each item enlisted in the agenda
To provide a basis for decision and action post meeting
questions.explanation: The agenda sets expectations prior to and during the meeting; it is the post-meeting minutes that document resolutions and track action items.

questions.question: Laissez-faire leadership style refers to a ______ style of leadership.
questions.explanation: Laissez-faire leadership grants complete autonomy and decision-making freedom to subordinates, known as delegative leadership.

questions.question: In which of the following styles of leadership does the leader motivate the subordinates primarily by the system of rewards and punishments?
questions.explanation: Transactional leadership relies on clear contractual incentives: positive rewards for goal attainment and penalties for performance failures.

questions.question: Who among the following is credited with the development of the Situational Leadership theory?
questions.explanation: Paul Hersey and Ken Blanchard formulated the Situational Leadership model, stating that effective leadership adapts to follower readiness.

assignments.title: Assignment 10
assignments.topic: Audience Interaction, Audio-Visual Aids & Delivery Modes

questions.question: Intelligent Aggressor people are reluctant to speak during interactive sessions so the best way to tackle them is to engage with them directly.
questions.explanation: Intelligent Aggressors are outspoken, assertive, and argumentative rather than reluctant. Tackling them involves firm boundaries and objective moderation.

questions.question: In order to make Submissive Recipients active participants, one can ask opinion-based questions, and stimulate independent thinking, etc.
questions.explanation: Inviting gentle, opinion-focused contributions in a safe atmosphere helps draw out shy or submissive audience members.

questions.question: Transitions are “statements in the body of the speech that lets the audience know what the speaker is going to discuss next.”
questions.explanation: Statements forecasting forthcoming points are 'internal previews'; transitions are connecting words that bridge previous thoughts to the next.

questions.question: A run-on sentence occurs when one sentence “runs” right into the next without proper punctuation between them.
questions.explanation: Run-on sentences occur when independent clauses are spliced together without appropriate terminal punctuation or coordinating conjunctions.

questions.question: Choose the incorrect pre-requisites for availing aid during a presentation:
options: Basic knowledge of the equipment is a must
Integration of aid with the presentation
Suitable location for the aid for easy accessibility and reach
questions.explanation: Visual media must be chosen deliberately to reinforce key concepts, rather than casually choosing 'any medium'.

questions.question: Choose the incorrect objective of audio-visual aids in the Education sector:
questions.explanation: Audio-visual media aims to stimulate curiosity, heighten engagement, and expand creative thinking, not neutralize creative sensibility.

questions.question: Speaking ______ is considered the most effective mode for a speaker.
questions.explanation: Extemporaneous speaking combines disciplined preparation with conversational flexibility, making it the most natural and effective delivery mode.

questions.question: ______ refer to brief statements to mark where one exactly is during a presentation.
questions.explanation: Signposts (e.g. 'First', 'Next', 'Turning now to...', 'In conclusion') are verbal cues that orient the audience within the speech structure.

questions.question: According to ______, “Leaders can no longer trust in power; instead, they rely on the power of trust.”
questions.explanation: Charles H. Green, noted author on trust-based leadership, highlighted that authentic leadership rests upon the power of earned trust.

questions.question: The ______ makes the decision guided by his/her expertise and knowledge and announces it to the group.
questions.explanation: In authoritative decision-making frameworks, the leader evaluates circumstances using personal expertise and communicates the mandate to the team.

questions.question: Who called language to be the instrument of “culture, domination and liberation”?
questions.explanation: British author and essayist Angela Carter characterized language as a potent medium of culture, hegemony, and liberation.

questions.question: Which linguistic function helps in strengthening social bonding?
questions.explanation: Phatic communication (small talk, pleasantries, greetings) serves to establish, warm, and maintain social bonds and interpersonal solidarity.

questions.question: According to Roman Jakobson, how many functions are there for a given language?
questions.explanation: Roman Jakobson's model identifies six functions of language: Referential, Emotive, Conative, Phatic, Metalingual, and Poetic.

questions.question: Who introduced the creative concept of “flow”?
questions.explanation: Positive psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi conceptualized 'flow' as a psychological state of complete, energized absorption in an activity.

questions.question: What is the term for a public presentation where several people present prepared speeches on different aspects of the same topic?
questions.explanation: A symposium brings together a panel of experts who deliver prepared addresses focusing on distinct aspects of a common subject.

questions.question: Which of the following is not one of the levels of politeness in communication?
questions.explanation: Sociolinguistic registers of politeness encompass formal/official, neutral, and informal/familiar; 'linear' is not a politeness level.

questions.question: Which two scholars propounded the linguistic relativity hypothesis? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Edward Sapir and Benjamin Lee Whorf developed the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis, arguing that language structures shape human cognition and cultural worldview.

questions.question: What are some of the factors which impair the clarity of speech? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Excessive technical jargon confuses uninitiated listeners, while doublespeak deliberately obfuscates meaning and distorts message clarity.

assignments.title: Assignment 12
assignments.topic: E-Learning, Panel Interviews & Digital Media Dynamics

questions.question: E-learning means all learning situations where there is significant use of ______ and communication resources.
questions.explanation: E-learning entails educational environments enriched and supported through informatics (information science and computation) and telecommunication technologies.

questions.question: When an interviewee is asked to tell his/her weakness/es, the ideal approach to answer this question is to describe your weakness as a ______ in disguise.
questions.explanation: Strategic interview practice involves acknowledging a genuine growth area while framing it as a constructive, evolving strength in disguise.

questions.question: In the setting of panel interview, the ______ usually begins the interview proceedings.
questions.explanation: The panel chair convenes the board, introduces the committee members, and formally initiates candidate questioning.

questions.question: Which of the following is not among the five determining factors of digital divide?
questions.explanation: Key dimensions analyzing the digital divide include access/availability, affordability, digital ability, and agency; 'acceptability' is not one of the five core determinants.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major challenge posed by the culture of online interaction?
questions.explanation: Data surveillance, personal confidentiality leaks, and erosion of digital privacy represent paramount concerns in online telecommunications.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct understanding of a panel interview?
questions.explanation: A panel interview is conducted by a group of multiple interviewers simultaneously interviewing a single candidate.

questions.question: Which of the following are the two most crucial and distinctive features of social media that have led to its increased significance? (select two)
questions.explanation: Dynamic real-time interactivity and omnipresent 24/7 mobile ubiquity are the defining drivers behind social media's worldwide impact.

questions.question: Select the two key roles played by Digital Media from the following options:
questions.explanation: In mass communication models, digital media functions decisively to communicate messages broadly and monitor public reactions.

questions.question: Which two of the following are not the characteristic features of online learning (E-Learning)?
questions.explanation: Modern e-learning promotes learner-centricity and interactive media, repudiating isolated contexts and unidirectional broadcast models.

questions.question: In an interview while answering a question on career history and future goals, which two of the following attitudes should one adopt?
questions.explanation: Hiring committees look for professional dedication (career-oriented vision) and vibrant enthusiasm (spirited energy).
